source_text: Ad Hebraeos ergo, ubi de generatione sermo est, ex uno dicuntur multi exstitisse, ad Romanos autem, ubi de peccato Apostolus loquitur, per unum hominem ait intrasse peccatum, quo numero absolutissime se nihil de generatione sensisse perdocuit.
pass_a_gloss: To the Hebrews therefore, where speech is about generation, many are said to have existed from one; but to the Romans, where the Apostle speaks about sin, he says sin entered through one human, by which number he taught most absolutely that he had sensed nothing about generation.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: In Hebrews, then, where generation is the subject, many are said to have arisen ‘from one.’ In Romans, however, where the apostle discusses sin, he says sin entered ‘through one man.’ By that number he taught with complete clarity that he meant nothing about generation.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
